criteria.reason: src/recipe/block.json has apiVersion 3, "render": "file:./render.php", "viewScriptModule": "file:./view.js" and supports.interactivity: true.
recipe-scaler.php calls register_block_type( __DIR__ . '/build/recipe' ) inside recipe_scaler_block_init, which is hooked to 'init'.
block.json defines title (string, default ''), servings (number, default 4) and ingredients (array of objects with quantity/unit/name, default []).

edit.js uses RichText for the title, __experimentalNumberControl as NumberControl inside InspectorControls/PanelBody for servings, and TextControl rows with add and remove buttons so ingredients can be edited.
view.js imports { store, getContext } from '@wordpress/interactivity' and calls store('recipe-scaler', …) with the derived getters scaledQuantity/isMinServings and the actions increment/decrement.
render.php puts data-wp-interactive="recipe-scaler" on the wrapper div.
render.php outputs the block context (baseServings, servings, ingredients) and the per-item index context with wp_interactivity_data_wp_context().
render.php wires the buttons with data-wp-on--click="actions.decrement" and data-wp-on--click="actions.increment".
render.php uses data-wp-text="context.servings" for the servings count and data-wp-text="state.scaledQuantity" for each quantity.
render.php puts data-wp-bind--disabled="state.isMinServings" on the − button, and view.js returns servings <= 1 for it.

render.php calls wp_interactivity_state('recipe-scaler', …) with closures for derived state that use wp_interactivity_get_context, and it also prints server-formatted fallback values for the count and quantities.
view.js formatQuantity uses Math.round((value + EPSILON) * 100) / 100, and PHP recipe_scaler_format_quantity rounds with round(..., 2).
render.php uses get_block_wrapper_attributes, esc_html, esc_attr_e, esc_html_e and wp_kses_post for the title, and runs sanitize_text_field on ingredient fields.

Every API used exists in WordPress or Gutenberg, including wp_interactivity_get_context, wp_interactivity_data_wp_context, Flex/FlexItem/FlexBlock and the __next40pxDefaultSize prop, so nothing is invented.
package.json lists @wordpress/scripts in devDependencies and its build/start scripts pass --experimental-modules.
